extracted.intended_audience: general readers (Reddit users, journalists, advertisers, researchers)
extracted.subtask_short: creating content and ads on Reddit
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for participating in, moderating, advertising on, and reporting about Reddit — including community norms, site-wide policies (e.g., bans, quarantines, doxxing), advertising etiquette, AMAs, and moderation/automation pitfalls. Useful for people planning to post, advertise, moderate, or research on Reddit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising etiquette on Reddit
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit's users dislike 'feeling manipulated by brands' but respond well to 'content that begs for intelligent viewers and participants.' 'Redditors don't want to advertise for you, they want to talk to you.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertisers should design promotions that 'spark conversations and feedback.' Use community-appropriate formats (e.g., AMAs) carefully, avoid appearing as covert advertising or astroturfing, and treat offbeat/irreverent questions as seriously as project-specific ones. Campaigns that appear inauthentic risk ridicule or backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-promotion and astroturfing prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-promotion is frowned upon; branded content made to appear as if it were original user content has been criticized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marketers should not 'infiltrate the reddit community on behalf of their brand.' Maintain transparency, avoid deceptive posts, and prefer strategies that genuinely engage users rather than pretend to be grassroots.

rubrics_metrics.name: AMA norms: honesty and authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: AMAs 'import the aspirational norms of honesty and authenticity from pseudonymous Internet forums into a public venue.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AMAs to get attention for public figures or products but approach carefully — authenticity is expected, and AMAs are 'not a fit for every project or client.' Moderators and participants expect truthful, open interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journalistic attribution and community ownership
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists are advised by the site's policies to respect that 'reddit's communities belong to their members' and to seek proper attribution for people's contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using Reddit content for reporting, seek permission/attribution and follow site guidelines about quoting or republishing user submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator discretion within site-wide rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The website grants subreddit moderators discretion in deciding what content is and is not allowed on their subreddits, so long as site-wide rules are not being violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect decentralized enforcement and variability across subreddits; individual communities can be highly moderated or permissive depending on moderators' choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-wide policy changes and enforcement (bans/quarantines)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit has changed its site-wide editorial policies several times; it has banned subreddits (e.g., jailbait, revenge porn, fatpeoplehate) and 'quarantined' communities with 'highly-offensive or upsetting content.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site-wide rule changes can lead to mass removals or quarantines; enforcement decisions may be controversial and can provoke community protests or blackouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doxxing / personally-identifying information rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit introduced a strict rule against the online publication of non-public personally-identifying information (doxxing); those who break the rule are subject to a site-wide ban and potential deletion of user-generated content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posting private personal data is a clear grounds for site-wide sanctions; moderators and admins enforce doxxing prohibitions strictly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hate speech and 'promoting hate' policy
rubrics_metrics.description: On June 29, 2020 Reddit updated its content policy and introduced rules aimed at curbing the presence of communities it believed to be 'promoting hate,' banning approximately 2,000 subreddits found in violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communities that systematically promote hate may be removed; these enforcement actions are politically sensitive and have drawn debate about free expression versus platform safety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brigading and coordinated manipulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit is vulnerable to disruptive or manipulative practices (troll farms, click farms, astroturfing) such as 'brigading'; these practices are against Reddit's content policy, though some historical examples were tacitly encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organized external campaigns to skew votes or polls are generally prohibited. Moderators and admins may take action, but historical context shows enforcement can be inconsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising review and ad safety limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Occasional advertiser content slips past human reviewers (example: WhiteDate ad encouraging white women to join ran and was later removed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ad review processes are not infallible; advertisers and platform reviewers must monitor campaigns and be prepared to remove problematic ads quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affiliate links / monetization practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit announced it would begin using VigLink to redirect affiliate links (June 2016).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetization tools such as affiliate redirects are in use; users and moderators may react to monetization choices depending on transparency and effect on user experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration and feature access rules (NSFW / posting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit can be viewed without an account but registration is required to submit, comment, or vote. Registration is also occasionally required to view posts marked as not safe for work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect some content or actions to be gated to registered users; community rules may additionally restrict access to certain topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated moderation pitfalls (AutoModerator misclassification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reddit's automatic moderation tools (AutoModerator) have misflagged content (example: flagging the word 'Luigi' as 'potentially violent'), leading to inappropriate warnings and moderation actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automated systems can produce false positives; moderators and admins should audit automated rules and be prepared to correct misclassifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform susceptibility to misinformation and echo chambers
rubrics_metrics.description: Due to decentralized moderation, user anonymity, and lack of fact-checking systems, the platform is highly prone to spreading misinformation and disinformation; users should exercise caution in taking unsourced content as fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly for medical information, unsourced posts can be dangerous — e.g., a study of UTI posts showed <1% cited sources and contained harmful misinformation. Content consumers and moderators should prioritize sourcing and fact-checking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research ethics and informed consent for experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: A University of Zurich study deployed AI-run Reddit accounts without moderator consent to influence opinions; critics argued the experiment was unethical due to impersonation and involuntary participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research that manipulates real communities should consider ethics, obtain consent or approval, and inform moderators and participants when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety / legal compliance (age verification for Online Safety Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: In July 2025, Reddit began requiring age verification to access certain features, to comply with the UK's Online Safety Act 2023, using a service called Persona. Content covered includes sexually explicit material, encouragement of suicide and eating disorders, and expressions of hatred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms must implement technical and policy measures (e.g., age checks) to comply with jurisdictional safety laws; this affects feature access and moderation workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform incident response and data protection concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: A February 2023 breach was claimed by the BlackCat hacker gang (80 GB exfiltrated); an FTC report found user and non-user data practices by companies (including Reddit) put individuals vulnerable to identity theft, stalking, discrimination, emotional distress, stigma, and reputational harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms must maintain robust security, respond transparently to breaches, and align data practices with regulatory expectations to reduce harms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderator/admin actions can provoke community protest
rubrics_metrics.description: Moderator removals, subreddit bans, or changes (e.g., firing of community managers, algorithm changes) have triggered large-scale blackouts and protests (e.g., 'AMAgeddon', moderators setting subreddits private).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platform policy or personnel changes may have large community impacts; administrators should anticipate moderator pushback and communication challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising via sponsored events and native ads
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 2017 Reddit has partnered with companies to host sponsored AMAs and other interactive events, increased advertising offerings, and introduced native mobile ads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsored events and native formats are available for advertisers but must be implemented in line with community norms and platform policies to avoid backlash.
